text.en: What if a poet used the Tamil language itself as the messenger?

Tamil Vidu Thoothu is a poem of the thoothu type, a short literary form (சிற்றிலக்கியம்) in which a messenger such as a parrot, swan or cloud carries a message. Here the poet makes Tamil itself the messenger, praising its sweetness, literary wealth, poetic variety, taste and beauty. Its opening lines call Tamil a sweet nectar and the fruit of liberation, and speak of the three Tamils: iyal, isai and nadakam (முத்தமிழ்).
The poem shows how a poet can express pride in the mother tongue. It presents Tamil as a language that can express every poetic form and every feeling, so people should love and protect it.
Notice the words தூது (a message), சிற்றிலக்கியம் (a minor genre of literature), முத்தமிழ் (three Tamils), பா வகைகள் (verse forms) and தேன் (honey, a metaphor for sweetness). This is a memorisation poem (மனப்பாடப் பகுதி) in the textbook.
